title: Defra PCM modelled background air pollution, 2024
description: Defra's Pollution Climate Mapping (PCM) model of 2024 annual mean background concentrations of nitrogen dioxide (NO2), PM10 and PM2.5 on a 1x1 km grid across the United Kingdom, with Defra's published population-weighted annual mean PM2.5 for each local authority.
publisher: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

files.note: PCM annual mean NO2 background map for 2024, µg m-3, from https://uk-air.defra.gov.uk/datastore/pcm/mapno22024.csv. Four header rows (pollutant, year, metric, units), a blank row, then gridcode, x, y and the value for each 1x1 km cell, with x and y the cell centre on the British National Grid: 254,905 cells covering the UK, Northern Ireland included.

PCM annual mean PM10 background map for 2024, µg m-3 in gravimetric units, from https://uk-air.defra.gov.uk/datastore/pcm/mappm102024g.csv. Same layout as the NO2 map; one cell off the west coast (gridcode 534070) is MISSING here and in the PM2.5 map but modelled for NO2.
PCM annual mean PM2.5 background map for 2024, µg m-3, from https://uk-air.defra.gov.uk/datastore/pcm/mappm252024g.csv. Same layout as the PM10 map.

Defra's population-weighted annual mean PM2.5 for 2024 for each of the 361 UK local authorities on April 2023 codes, as total, non-anthropogenic and anthropogenic concentrations, from https://uk-air.defra.gov.uk/datastore/pcm/popwmpm252024byUKlocalauthority.csv. Defra advises the total for health burden calculations.

Built by scripts/compile-air-quality.mts from the three PCM maps: each cell is given to the December 2024 local authority (generalised clipped boundaries) containing its centre, brought from the British National Grid through EPSG:1314, and an authority's value is the unweighted mean of its cells, the average background concentration across its area. Every authority receives cells, the fewest being the City of London's 3; 10,626 coastal cells whose centres fall offshore of the generalised coastline are assigned to none. These area means are not population weighted: against Defra's population-weighted PM2.5 they correlate at 0.995 and run 0.21 µg m-3 lower on average, most in large rural authorities where people live in the more polluted places.
